claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element alloy with nearly equiatomic principal-element ratios.
The starting catalyst contains low amounts of platinum-group metals.
The starting catalyst loses activity under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions involving H2O and NO.
The starting catalyst degrades during thermal aging or increasing simulated mileage.

A closed-loop workflow combining automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated aging, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimization can refine catalyst composition and processing conditions.
Closed-loop optimization will identify beneficial slight deviations from equiatomic element ratios.
Deviating from strict equiatomic ratios will modify elemental distributions.
The optimized composition and processing conditions will stabilize multiphase microstructures.
Modified elemental distributions and stabilized multiphase microstructures will improve resistance to sintering.
Modified elemental distributions and stabilized multiphase microstructures will improve resistance to poisoning and phase degradation.
Slight compositional and processing modifications will favor durable, catalytically active surface phases.
Slight compositional and processing modifications will promote protective self-passivating surface layers.
The proposed active phases and passivating layers will resist degradation caused by H2O, NO, and thermal stress.
The proposed optimization can achieve stabilization without increasing platinum-group-metal loading.
The optimized catalyst will retain more catalytic activity than the untreated nearly equiatomic catalyst.
The optimized catalyst will be more durable than the untreated nearly equiatomic catalyst under harsh transient exhaust conditions.
The optimized catalyst will maintain minimal precious-metal use.
The intervention may fail when degradation is dominated by mechanisms not mitigated by elemental redistribution.
Scale-up and reproducibility across real-world operating conditions remain unvalidated.
